title: IBGE employer business survival: 2017 cohort observed through 2022

latest_release_verification.status: 2022 is the latest year listed in this official FTP product directory on acquisition; not a guarantee about other products

definitions.employer_enterprises: Enterprises with at least one salaried employee on 31 December; national enterprise statistics, not all registered businesses.
definitions.employer_local_units: Employer establishments/local units; distinct from enterprises. State comparisons use this population and its own Brazil comparator.
definitions.birth: Employer births include new activity, activity restarted after over 24 months of inactivity, and existing enterprises entering employer status after at least 24 months without employees.
definitions.survival: Active as an employer in birth year and each consecutive observation year; losing employer status can end survival without legal business closure.
definitions.births: Published 2017 cohort denominator for the same population and group as the rate. Not the 2022 count of active businesses.
definitions.size: Published salaried-personnel bands; association with survival is descriptive, not causal.
definitions.curve: Published percentages for ages 1-5, fixed 2017 cohort. No inferred count of survivors is supplied.

sector_standardisation.method: Direct descriptive standardisation: sum over common-support sectors of (Brazil 2017 local-unit birth share among included sectors * state published sector five-year survival percentage). Same national weights for every state. No invented rate for absent sectors.
sector_standardisation.scope: Employer local units only. Adjusts CNAE-section birth-cohort composition only; no size, municipality, founder, or firm-level adjustment; no causal or predictive model. Rankings are descriptive sensitivity diagnostics, not location recommendations.
sector_standardisation.raw_common_method: State sector-birth-weighted average of published rates over exactly the included sectors; rates retain published rounding.
sector_standardisation.rank_convention: Rank 1 is highest descriptive survival percentage; positive rank change means movement toward rank 1. No statistical significance is implied.

limitations: Published aggregate tables provide no individual enterprise histories, municipality survival estimates, founder covariates, or fitted adjusted survival model.
State rankings describe employer local units, while national enterprise sector/size comparisons describe employer enterprises; do not combine their denominators.
Five-year rates cover the pandemic period but alone do not identify a causal pandemic effect.
Rates retain workbook precision; publication text typically rounds to one decimal. No invented uncertainty intervals or reconstructed survivor counts.
Small sector denominators require care: electricity/gas has 119 enterprise births, public administration 7; display denominators alongside comparisons.

PDF size-section heading says local units, but its body and Chart 3 say enterprises; Table 2.1 size groups sum to the 261302-enterprise cohort. Table 2.1 title contains extraneous salary/age wording; extracted columns are births and survival rates only.
